Theme 087 · Art movements & eras

Cut-Paper Title Sequence

A mid-century opening-titles treatment in the spirit of Saul Bass: flat fields of colour, hand-cut paper strips with ragged edges, jaunty hand-set words and credits-style captions. The dashboards are sliding paper bars, the pulse line is a cut strip that zigzags across the screen, and the anomaly is a bar that snaps and falls away.

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

The coral paper disc rolls in from the right, the headline words pop in on quarter notes with jitter, and the teal CTA strip is slid in from the left on the final hit.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Cut-paper strip — rectangles with jittered 28 px edges — bars, rules, buttons
  • Zigzag pulse strip — one paper cut-out forming the heartbeat line
  • Jaunty title words — each word rotated ±2.5° and offset ±6 px
  • Credits caption — tracked uppercase Manrope 600 in title-card style
  • Torn bar — the anomaly: a bar ripped in two, top piece falling in coral
  • Paper disc — hand-cut circle for the coral dot or accents

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Stop-motion hold — animate on 2s or 3s (12 or 8 fps) with 1–2 px jitter per frame to sell hand-made paper
  • Slide & snap — strips slide from off-frame, power2.out 0.3 s, then a 3-frame overshoot, one per 8th note
  • Tear & tumble — torn piece rotate 0→24° and y +120 px, power2.in 0.5 s; tear lands on a downbeat with a paper-rip SFX

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Title-sequence grammar makes a product film feel authored and cinematic, and cut paper keeps data warm instead of clinical. Risk: it can read as retro pastiche; the hand-made jitter must stay subtle so numbers remain crisp.

Adapt to your product: Rebuild your product's key chart or UI element as paper cut-outs and let the moment your product acts be a single cut, tear or snap. Your CTA becomes the final credit card.

References: https://www.artofthetitle.com/designer/saul-bass/ — Art of the Title: Saul Bass title sequences (The Man with the Golden Arm, Anatomy of a Murder, Vertigo) · https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saul_Bass — Bass's cut-paper animation and kinetic typography
